ESETISMERTETÉS
CASE REPORT OF A WOMAN WITH ANTI AMPHIPHYSIN
POSITIVE STIFF PERSON SYNDROME
A 68 year old woman who was unable to walk because of a history of five days long painful lower limb spasms was presented to a neurology department of a district hospital in January 2011.
In the one-year follow-up examination the status of the patient was stable.

A 68 year old woman who was unable to walk because of a history of five days long painful lower limb spasms was presented to a neurology department of a district hospital in January 2011. [...] Before cancer screening was started, an intrathecal baclofen pump must have been implantated for symptomatic treatment, because the patient suffered heavily from painful spasms which also made impossible her proper further examination. [...] Serum GAD test was negative. A 68 year old woman who was unable to walk because of a history of five days long painful lower limb spasms was presented to a neurology department of a district hospital in January 2011. Upon admission the patella reflexes were brisk, Babinski sign was positive on both sides. The trunk and the lower limbs were extremely spastic (Asworth 4 on both sides), with continuous painful extensor spasms.
